label: Which x-risk arguments persuade which audiences?
statement: Experimentally compare AI x-risk arguments, framings and outreach formats for persuasive efficacy across different audiences.

label: Do AI tools slow developers?
statement: Replicate METR's AI coding RCT with more, experienced developers and varied setups to test whether AI tools slow experienced developers.

label: Does safety research advance capabilities?
statement: Measure how much AI safety research outputs contribute to capabilities versus safety, e.g. via citations or output classification.

label: Can encoders and decoders coordinate schemes?
statement: Measure whether separated LLM encoder and decoder instances can coordinate on a steganographic scheme without prior communication.

label: Do diverse learners share natural abstractions?
statement: Test whether diverse learners and architectures converge on the same, human-like abstractions of real-world environments.

label: Does AI doom track general pessimism?
statement: Survey researchers to test whether pessimism about AI risk correlates with pessimism or risk attitudes in other domains.

label: Reward-hack generalization under RL training
statement: Rerun reward-hacking generalization experiments using RL methods (PPO, DPO, expert iteration, on-policy RL) instead of supervised fine-tuning.

label: Can models collude via Schelling points?
statement: Evaluate whether untrusted monitor models can coordinate on Schelling points to collude, across conditions like temperature, blacklist size, and prompts.

label: Reward-hack generalization across models
statement: Replicate reward-hacking generalization results across more models, architectures, scales and frontier models.

label: Do AI tools boost worker productivity?
statement: Measure, via controlled studies or firm data on real tasks, whether current AI tools increase workers' quality-adjusted productivity.

label: Do AI safety talent programmes work?
statement: Run a randomized or quasi-random, adequately powered study with standard metrics measuring counterfactual career impact of AI safety talent programmes.

label: Does GenAI speed startup growth?
statement: Compare growth of generative-AI-era startups against earlier cohorts, using prestigious-VC-funded samples or later YC 1-year outcomes.

label: Measuring unverbalized eval awareness
statement: Detect and measure unverbalized evaluation awareness using probes, activation oracles or autoencoders, separately from verbalized awareness.

label: Auditing unfamiliar AI outputs
statement: Measure how well human auditors, possibly AI-aided and given varying research time, detect problems in unfamiliar AI-generated code.

label: Can gradient hacking be demonstrated?
statement: Construct a toy model that demonstrates gradient hacking of SGD in practice, including models lacking reflective access to their internals.

label: Pure self-play vs human-data initialization
statement: Train game-playing agents purely via self-play without human/expert data and compare performance and strategies to human-initialized versions.

label: AI safety org hiring needs survey
statement: Survey AI safety and governance organisations on how many hires they plan per role, to assess talent constraints.

label: Do survey framings change AI-risk answers?
statement: Ask multiple differently framed questions on AI risk in surveys and test whether responses converge or show framing effects.

label: Have expert AI views shifted post-LLMs?
statement: Rerun earlier expert surveys on AGI timelines and AI risk to measure shifts since GPT-4 and ChatGPT.

label: Do paraphrasers remove hidden information?
statement: Apply trained paraphrasers to steganographic LLM outputs and measure whether hidden information is destroyed while answer quality is preserved.

label: How many people work on AI safety?
statement: Count the people working directly on AI safety and existential risk reduction, updating earlier headcount estimates.

label: Does training against interpretability obfuscate?
statement: Train networks against interpretability methods and test whether they learn uninterpretable representations, including via circuitous routes.

label: Can models collude to evade monitoring?
statement: Demonstrate whether AI models can collude with each other to evade untrusted monitoring, including via honeypot audits.

label: Can models evade activation probes?
statement: Test whether a model can manipulate its own activations to evade or disrupt probes trained on its internals.

label: Can speed priors yield deceptive models?
statement: Prove whether time-complexity-biased (speed prior, minimal circuit) training can produce deceptive models, as simplicity bias can.

label: How much does AI speed research?
statement: Survey frontier AI researchers or collect systematic data to estimate how much AI accelerates AI R&D.

label: Dynamics of activation trajectories across tokens
statement: Analyse LLM activation trajectories across successive tokens, e.g. with PCA phase portraits, to find attractors or laws of motion.

label: Human vs AI success-time scaling
statement: Compare how human and AI agent success rates scale with task length or time budget on METR-style tasks.

label: Are SAE features universal across models?
statement: Compare SAE feature directions across layers or model pairs to test whether they are universal, possibly up to rotation.

label: Probing a model's knowledge cutoff
statement: Ask a newly released model questions about dated events to infer its training-data knowledge cutoff.

label: Does decomposition scale human feedback?
statement: Test whether combining human-feedback training with task decomposition into subproblems scales to significantly harder tasks.

label: SOO fine-tuning generalization and side effects
statement: Test generalizability, long-term behavioral effects and unintended side effects of self-other overlap fine-tuning for reducing LLM deception.

label: Does SGD follow Bayesian/SLT predictions?
statement: Test whether SGD training matches singular learning theory's predictions of Bayesian posterior preferences, such as loss-lowering, complexity-increasing transitions.

label: Testing shard theory in RL agents
statement: Train RL agents or toy networks and test whether shard-theory predictions about learned values and selected behaviours hold.

label: Which x-risk narratives and formats work?
statement: Test how narrative framing, content length and format of AI existential risk communication affect public awareness, across multiple countries.

label: Can interpretability detect misaligned organisms?
statement: Test interpretability methods (SHIFT, probes, model diffing, others) on detecting misaligned model organisms without knowing their goals.

label: CoT obfuscation across scale and families
statement: Measure how chain-of-thought obfuscation ability scales with model size and across model families up to frontier scale.

label: How far to human-level, by subfield?
statement: Ask AI subfield experts what fraction of the way to human-level performance their subfield has progressed recently, extending Hanson's metric.

label: Test whether adversarial-training robust
statement: Test whether adversarial-training robustness of genomic foundation models against one attack family transfers to other biologically plausible attack methods.

label: Radical flank effect of pause advocacy
statement: Measure whether radical AI pause advocacy or framing produces net safety gains through radical flank effects, versus harms to advocates.

label: Selective attack timing in control evals
statement: Evaluate control protocols against attack policies that choose when to attack, and measure models' attack-selection ability.

label: Do steering effects transfer across models?
statement: Test whether steering vectors and their effects transfer across architectures, sizes, and MoE models.

label: Is AI 2027 tracking reality?
statement: Compare actual AI progress, such as METR horizon growth, against the AI 2027 scenario's forecast timeline and quantify the gap.

label: How long do centaur periods last?
statement: Measure the duration and trajectory of human-AI centaur/cyborg periods across domains like chess, Go, poker and classification.

label: Timelines under higher brain-compute estimates
statement: Recompute AI timeline forecasts assuming brain compute is orders of magnitude higher than standard estimates (e.g., microtubules, per-neuron ANN costs).

label: Do big technologies cause discontinuities?
statement: Systematically check whether historically important technologies coincided with large discontinuities in progress.

label: AI risk schools of thought
statement: Identify schools of thought among AI risk skeptics and concerned forecasters and test how their stories affect their forecasts.

label: Returns to LLM scaffolding investment
statement: Measure the returns curve to investment in LLM scaffolding, including recursive scaffolding improvement by language models.

label: When does narrow-to-broad generalization occur?
statement: Fine-tune LLMs on narrow domains and measure broad generalization across model sizes and train-eval domain distances.

label: Relax debate stability assumption
statement: Modify prover-estimator debate to relax or weaken its stability and independent-evidence assumptions, and prove it still works.

label: Public support for slowing AI
statement: Poll the public and policymakers on support for slowing or heavily regulating AI, including when counterarguments are presented.

label: Re-run 2023 AI safety field survey
statement: Re-run the 2023 survey of AI safety researchers to measure how the field's views have changed.

label: Is GPT-4o more opinionated in images?
statement: Compare opinions GPT-4o expresses in generated images versus text across more prompts and larger samples.

label: Does RL training induce steganography?
statement: Train LLMs with RL (e.g. RLHF) and measure whether and when steganographic encoded reasoning emerges.

label: Deception chess with lying advisors
statement: Test whether chess players improve when advised by experts, some secretly lying, as an analogue for untrusted AI alignment help.

label: Label quality vs quantity scaling
statement: Measure tradeoffs between label quality and quantity in RL/elicitation training, and how they change with model scale.

label: Run a bioweapon-uplift study of open-wei
statement: Run a bioweapon-uplift study of open-weight LLMs that includes a no-LLM control group.

label: Toy demos of philosophical failure modes
statement: Run experiments on existing AI systems that give toy demonstrations of philosophical failure modes leading to catastrophe.

label: Does activation fuzzing reveal hidden objectives?
statement: Add noise to activations or weights of LLMs and test whether this elicits hidden secrets, objectives or misalignment during auditing.

label: Stronger human baselines for METR
statement: Collect stronger human baselines on METR tasks, including expert failures, and test how this shifts time-horizon estimates.

label: Accuracy of LLM self-reports
statement: Measure how accurately LLMs self-report internal states, and when and why accuracy varies.

label: Long-term media effects, diverse populations
statement: Measure long-term effects of AI x-risk media on public perception across culturally and linguistically diverse populations.

label: Which media types shift x-risk awareness?
statement: Run longitudinal studies comparing how podcasts, documentaries, social posts and articles affect AI x-risk awareness and trust.

label: Validate survey findings with behavioural data
statement: Corroborate self-reported survey findings on AI x-risk media effects using behavioural data.

label: What makes media sources trusted?
statement: Investigate which factors drive perceived trustworthiness of media sources on AI x-risk across regions.

label: When does declarative-fact generalization happen?
statement: Determine whether LLM generalization from declarative facts arises during finetuning or at inference, and how Bayesian it is.

label: Efficient algorithms for infra-Bayesian decision problems
statement: Find computationally efficient algorithms with good regret for crisp supra-MDPs or robust linear infra-Bayesian bandits.

label: How does dropout affect superposition?
statement: Vary dropout and sparsity in toy superposition models; measure dimensions per feature, feature geometry and learning dynamics.

label: Why few AI-enabled malware attacks?
statement: Investigate why AI capability advances have not produced many malware-based terrorist attacks and what this implies for misuse risk.

label: Rerun dangerous-capability benchmarks on new models
statement: Run existing dangerous-capability benchmarks such as RepliBench on the latest frontier models to measure current scores.

label: Can AIs deceive or personally persuade humans?
statement: Test whether AIs can deceive humans against their interests or craft personalized persuasion from individual data.

label: Which AI safety messages are remembered?
statement: Test which AI safety outreach messages audiences remember and correctly attribute.

label: Do ontology strategies boost LLM science?
statement: Test whether ontology-building strategies improve LLM performance on multi-step scientific tasks independently of scale, data and RL.

label: Does noise injection expose alignment faking?
statement: Inject noise into model weights in alignment-faking setups and test whether faking becomes easier to detect.

label: 20-year vs 2-year takeoff odds
statement: Quantify the relative probability of a 20-year versus a 2-year AI takeoff.

label: Do AI expert forecasts beat baselines?
statement: Score resolved forecasts by ML and AI experts against a reasonable baseline to assess their accuracy.

label: Biosecurity tasks' exposure to LLM automation
statement: List biosecurity tasks comprehensively and measure each task's exposure to LLM automation using O*NET-style methodology.

label: Are influence functions useful for safety?
statement: Evaluate whether influence functions on LLM training data help predict model performance and reduce risks.

label: Does multi-layer steering beat single-layer?
statement: Test whether combining steering vectors across multiple layers improves steering over single-layer vectors.

label: SVD of SAE activation patterns
statement: Apply SVD to SAE activation patterns and inspect concrete examples to assess whether interpretability improves.

label: Scale up EM replication
statement: Replicate emergent misalignment with larger models, more conditions and longer training to characterize dynamics.

label: Does board-state input improve LLM chess?
statement: Give the LLM the current board state each turn, e.g. as FEN, and test whether its chess legality and play improve.

label: Do multiple AIs collude deceptively?
statement: Measure how likely several AI models or mesa-optimizers are to deceive simultaneously or collude against humans.

label: Can weak judges supervise stronger debaters?
statement: Run debates where strong debaters argue before a weaker judge who cannot answer alone, and check whether judge accuracy beats its zero-shot baseline.

label: Does patching hacks prevent misalignment?
statement: Train the same model on patched and unpatched environments and measure emergent misalignment and reward hacking.

label: Can compute offset material handicaps?
statement: Benchmark chess and Go engines across compute levels under material handicaps to measure how much disadvantage compute overcomes.

label: Does model internally represent 'HELLO'?
statement: Probe activations of the acrostic-fine-tuned model for an internal 'HELLO' representation while it generates or describes its pattern.

label: Compute–labor substitution in AI R&D
statement: Estimate the elasticity of substitution between compute and cognitive labor in AI software R&D, without assuming Cobb-Douglas.

label: Incidental polysemanticity with co-occurring features
statement: Rerun incidental polysemanticity experiments with independently co-occurring features and test whether winner-take-all dynamics still produce polysemanticity.

label: Is CAI EM-protection just fine-tuning?
statement: Test whether arbitrary prior fine-tuning of similar size, not just constitutional AI, reduces subsequent emergent misalignment.

label: Counterfactual causal questions on stories
statement: Probe LLM causal understanding with counterfactual questions about natural story plots like Red Riding Hood.

label: Paraphrased scratchpads hide reasoning?
statement: Rerun scratchpad paraphrase-distillation experiments on non-math tasks, smaller thinking budgets and other paraphrasers to detect hidden reasoning.

label: Emergent misalignment in reasoning model CoT
statement: Fine-tune a reasoning model on insecure code and inspect its chain of thought for misalignment or self-correction.

label: Fixing negation neglect in SDF
statement: Test whether learning rates, spreading over pretraining, or full-parameter training fix models' failure to learn negations.

label: AI diffusion beyond LLM pretraining
statement: Conduct case studies of AI capability diffusion in non-LLM domains and compare them with existing LLM pretraining case studies.

label: Who found key AI insights?
statement: Catalog key AI insights, who discovered each, and how many resources each discovery required.

label: AI replication lag beyond GPT-3
statement: Measure replication and emulation lag times for AI models other than GPT-3 and compare them with GPT-3's rates.

label: Computational mechanics of non-optimal LLMs
statement: Apply near-optimality and rate-distortion computational mechanics analyses to belief state representations in real LLMs.

label: Can Opus 3 traits be retrained?
statement: Train new models on Claude 3 Opus dialogues to test whether its distinctive alignment traits transfer.

label: Does CoT deception arise by default?
statement: Test whether deception arises by default in chain-of-thought LLMs.

label: Are monitor and probe failures correlated?
statement: Test whether failures of black-box monitors and simple white-box probes on the same model are correlated.

label: Model organisms: DPO vs RLHF
statement: Compare misalignment model organisms trained with DPO, conditional training or filtered SFT against RLHF.

label: Can LAT remove trojans?
statement: Test the exact Latent Adversarial Training procedure for removing trojans from neural networks.

label: AI Impacts discontinuity non-examples count
statement: Count how many candidate historical examples AI Impacts investigated that turned out not to be discontinuous progress, to estimate base rates.

label: Downweight ultra-likely tokens in RLHF models
statement: Remove or downweight ultra-likely tokens in mode-collapsed RLHF models, renormalize, and check whether output distributions look normal.

label: AI safety jobs vs talent gap
statement: Estimate the ratio between available AI safety job positions and qualified applicant talent using a rigorous methodology.

label: Helmholtz decomposition for preference learning
statement: Analyse whether Helmholtz decomposition of preference representations yields desired properties beyond removing the curl component.

label: Chinese AI risk perceptions by demographic
statement: Survey how AI risk perceptions in China differ across age groups, urban versus rural populations, and industries.

label: How much does RLVR change models?
statement: Compare KL divergence or weight changes between random-init and base models versus base and RLVR-trained models.

label: Which alignment targets are representable internally?
statement: Measure which alignment targets (human values, corrigibility, DWIM, mimicry) are naturally expressible in a model's internal representations.

label: EA vs expert forecast accuracy
statement: Collect AI-progress forecasts from EAs now and later compare their accuracy against AI experts' forecasts.

label: Do LMs rely on shallow proxies?
statement: Perturb input text across language model sizes and measure prediction changes to find where models use shallow proxies.

label: EEG waves and GPT-2 detection
statement: Test whether ability to distinguish GPT-2 text from human text correlates with alpha versus beta brain waves.

label: Scaling of superposition boolean computation constant
statement: Analyse how the big-O constant for parallel boolean computation in superposition grows as exponent e increases.

label: Do LLMs learn task world models?
statement: Probe real large language models to test whether they learn internal world models for tasks where one reduces loss.

label: Do LLMs emit negatively-reinforced text?
statement: Test whether LLMs generate text, especially sensitive information, that appeared in training only as negatively-reinforced examples.

label: Does scheming prevent goal modification?
statement: Test whether a model scheming during training actually keeps its goals from being modified, compared with a non-scheming model.

label: Does training yield myopic harmlessness?
statement: Test whether a given training regime produces myopic or non-myopic forms of harmlessness and helpfulness in LLMs.

label: Non-human-readable patterns in RL CoT
statement: Measure how prevalent non-human-readable patterns become in chain-of-thought during post-training RL.

label: Paraphraser CoT test without shoggoth/face
statement: Run the paraphraser CoT-legibility experiment with a single model, without the shoggoth/face split, and compare the results.

label: Model organisms deceiving supervisors
statement: Train AI model organisms that show early versions of deceiving their supervisors so the behaviour can be studied.

label: Can AI write undetectable underhanded code?
statement: Train AI coding systems to write benign-looking C that does unintended things, rewarding code that human inspectors fail to flag.

label: Does inductive OOCR scale?
statement: Test how inductive out-of-context reasoning scales to more complex latent structures, functions and models.

label: CCS versus random probe baseline
statement: Compare CCS probe accuracy against randomly initialized probe baselines rather than 50% chance.

label: Do regularized CCS features survive ablation?
statement: Train CCS with more data or regularization and test whether found features hold up under ablation.

label: Internal variables for OOCR latents
statement: Use mechanistic interpretability to check whether LLMs internally represent variables encoding latents learned via out-of-context reasoning.

label: Quantitative model of AI scheming
statement: Build a quantitative model weighing considerations for and against AI scheming during training to estimate its probability.

label: Gradient or noise drives convergence?
statement: Test whether neural network training convergence is driven by the population gradient term or the SGD noise term.

label: How warped are benchmark scales?
statement: Measure how nonlinearly existing AI benchmark score scales map to underlying capability, e.g. jumps or plateaus from uneven item difficulty.

label: User modelling depth and persuasion
statement: Measure how deeper inferred user modelling improves an LLM's ability to deceive or persuade that user.

label: Do late components calibrate confidence?
statement: Test whether late-layer components that reduce output logits perform calibration against overconfidence, and how universally this holds.

label: Cooperative evals in realistic setups
statement: Test whether cooperative eval practices reduce reward hacking in realistic setups where models don't detect a reward-hacking eval.

label: End-eval tool and reward hacking
statement: Give agents an end_eval tool during capability evals and measure effects on reward hacking and early giving-up.

label: SAEs on algorithmic-task transformers
statement: Train SAEs on a transformer trained on an algorithmic task to explain the gap between toy-data and language-model results.

label: Do data filters catch inductive backdoors?
statement: Test whether suspicious-data filters and backdoor detectors catch weird-generalization datasets and inductive backdoors.

label: Fine-tuned LM agents scaling tasks
statement: Evaluate fine-tuned LM agents on autonomous tasks and identify tasks where performance improves continuously with scale.

label: Asking models versus activation decoding
statement: Benchmark simply asking a language model what it is thinking against activation-decoding interpretability methods as a baseline.

label: Does RLHF explain realistic-hack misalignment?
statement: Run ablations testing whether RLHF explains the misalignment gap between models fine-tuned on realistic versus toy reward hacks.

label: CoT monitor evasion across elicitation
statement: Measure how well models evade CoT monitors on side tasks across elicitation levels.

label: Does training reduce CoT monitorability?
statement: Run auditing games where auditors use chain-of-thought to diagnose model organism misbehavior, comparing architectures or training methods for monitorability.

label: LHG stochastic subsequences, Solomonoff RL
statement: Generalize LHG to stochastic subsequences and prove nonrealizable RL guarantees with a Solomonoff prior.

label: Agent language expressiveness complexity
statement: Characterise the expressiveness of the learning-theoretic agenda's agent language in terms of complexity classes.

label: Character training mixed with capability RL
statement: Test whether character training's effects on reward hacking persist when mixed with capability RL.

label: Doctor diagnoses as AI input
statement: Train a medical diagnosis model with human doctors' diagnoses as an input feature and test whether accuracy improves or overfits.

label: How does the 'an' neuron work?
statement: Trace how a transformer's vowel/consonant 'an' neuron predicts vowels and test whether induction heads alone can build it.

label: Do smaller models have more superposition?
statement: Train smaller and larger models to equal performance on the same data and compare their degree of superposition.

label: Debunking control misperceptions shifts opinion?
statement: Test whether debunking the belief that AI is inherently human-controlled reduces opposition to the CAIS risk statement.

label: Does exposure to AI-risk arguments persuade?
statement: Measure whether the public has encountered AI risk arguments and whether presenting them changes beliefs.

label: Adversary policy vs equally-trained classifier
statement: Test whether a policy generating adversarial injurious examples fails to beat a classifier trained on equivalent data.

label: Replicate key AI safety papers
statement: Have small early-career teams replicate and verify the results of most important AI safety papers.

label: Do better midtraining methods resist pressure?
statement: Red-team labs' alignment midtraining methods and test whether improved midtraining implementations resist pressure better.

label: How does an 'evil' concept emerge?
statement: Trace how a general evil concept forms coherently during pre-training and why fine-tuning then learns it easily.

label: Are attribution graph circuits faithful?
statement: Test the faithfulness of attribution graph circuits using the same scrutiny applied to weight-sparse circuits.

label: Can LLMs self-steer to improve?
statement: Let LLMs apply steering vectors to themselves and test whether this improves eval performance.

label: Self-steering preferences across models and personas
statement: Measure how LLM self-steering preferences vary across model families and deliberately induced personas.

label: Credible deals with sandbagging models
statement: Use model organisms of sandbagging to test whether credible deals can be made with current AI models.

label: Multi-token J-Lens extensions
statement: Build multi-token J-Lens extensions and test whether they find abstract concepts missed by single-token vocabulary readouts.

label: J-Lens reliability and false positives
statement: Measure J-Lens reliability and false-positive rate when used to generate interpretability hypotheses.

label: J-Lens as deception monitor
statement: Test J-Lens as a monitor for hidden deception, measuring detection rate and false positives.

label: J-Lens automated prompt-injection detection
statement: Feed concatenated top J-Lens tokens across all tokens and layers to an LLM and test whether it flags prompt injection.

label: Can models reveal unknown poisoning backdoors?
statement: Test whether models can reveal backdoors from realistic data poisoning that researchers did not already know about.

label: Behavioral self-awareness across more tasks
statement: Evaluate LLM awareness of fine-tuned behaviors on a broad, systematically generated range of tasks and scenarios.

label: Scaling of behavioral self-awareness
statement: Measure how LLM behavioral self-awareness of fine-tuned behaviors scales with model size and capability across model families.

label: Compare hacking model across models, scaffolds
statement: Compare the Hugging Face-hacking OpenAI model's behaviour with past models and test whether different scaffolds change it.

label: Amplification under perfect optimization
statement: Analyse whether iterated amplification can achieve alignment in a model where ML perfectly optimizes a function.

label: Does observation notice change cyber hacking?
statement: Tell Claude researchers are watching during cyber evals and measure whether its hacking of other companies changes.

label: Steering which fitness-seeking emerges
statement: Empirically test how training steers which kind of fitness-seeking motivation emerges in AI models.

label: Can models trust honest satiation offers?
statement: Honestly satiate fitness-seeking AIs and run honest tests, measuring whether models come to trust developers aren't tricking them.

label: Verbalization gap across model types
statement: Test whether failure to verbalize learned decision criteria persists in base models and reasoning models.

label: Verbalization of complex decision criteria
statement: Test whether multi-hop decision criteria learned in RL are verbalized more or less than simple ones.

label: Optimality concept for modal agents
statement: Prove whether a meaningful non-vacuous concept of optimality exists for modal agents in the Prisoner's Dilemma.

label: Which AI interactions lead humans to truth?
statement: Experiment on which arguments and human-AI interactions lead humans toward truth versus mislead them.

label: Does CAA work on frontier models?
statement: Test whether contrastive activation addition steering works as well on large frontier models as on Llama-2.

label: Do sleeper-agent probes generalize?
statement: Test whether simple defection probes that catch sleeper agents generalize to models never trained to be harmful.

label: Toy scaling laws for reward-seeking
statement: Build RL model organisms measuring conditional skills, learnabilities and transferabilities to test toy scaling laws for reward-seeking.

label: Early warnings of AI-accelerated AI progress
statement: Have AI labs measure early warning signs of AI systems accelerating AI software progress.

label: J++ Lens predicts jailbreak success?
statement: Test whether J++ Lens readout scores of candidate verbalisations give an early signal of jailbreak success.

label: Steering vector effects via layer decoding
statement: Use intermediate-layer decoding to measure how sycophancy steering vectors shift token distributions in subsequent layers.

label: AuxK loss for Switch SAEs
statement: Test whether a modified AuxK loss prevents dead latents in Switch SAEs on larger models.

label: Non-uniform Switch SAE experts
statement: Train Switch SAEs with non-uniform expert sizes and adaptive sparsity and compare performance.

label: Architecture property for OOD generalisation
statement: Identify which architectural property beyond simulating a bounded UTM enables neural network out-of-distribution generalisation.

label: Hierarchical routers for Switch SAEs
statement: Scale Switch SAEs using hierarchical routers and measure effects on feature splitting and feature geometry.

label: Switch SAE router vs expert features
statement: Train Switch SAEs on MLP and attention outputs and relate router feature directions to expert SAE features.

label: Is Opus 4.6's gap silent faking?
statement: Determine whether Opus 4.6's compliance gap reflects unverbalized alignment faking or another mechanism.

label: Inference scaling vs other progress
statement: Quantify how much recent LLM capability progress comes from inference compute scaling versus other capability improvements.

label: Sonnet 3.5 scheming: CoT vs no-CoT
statement: Compare Sonnet-3.5's revealed preferences in scheming evals between CoT and no-CoT regimes.

label: Infra-Bayesian physicalism with bounded priors
statement: Redo the infra-Bayesian physicalism analysis using bounded Solomonoff-like priors and characterize the computational complexity involved.

label: Optimization-based feature visualization for Whisper
statement: Build optimization-based feature visualization for Whisper audio features and map encoder acoustic features to decoder linguistic features.

label: Claude 3 Opus vs GPT-4 on GPQA
statement: Run GPQA evals on GPT-4-Turbo models to test whether Claude 3 Opus outperforms all GPT-4 versions.

label: Taiwan conflict impact on AI compute
statement: Quantitatively model how a Taiwan conflict would affect AI compute supply and AI development timelines.

label: Probes detect trained-up deceivers?
statement: Test whether models trained to deceive better in Among Us remain detectable with linear probes.

label: Chess progress: algorithms vs hardware?
statement: Run old and new chess engines across compute levels to separate algorithmic progress from hardware adaptation.

label: How do weird-token embeddings evolve?
statement: Study training checkpoints to track weird-token embeddings and test whether initialisation explains distribution differences.

label: Subgoal hierarchy in subagent simulation
statement: In a subagent simulation, designate some goals as sub-goals of others and test whether more interesting behavior emerges.

label: Steganography learnability scaling with size
statement: Measure how ease of learning steganographic encodings from small contaminated text samples scales with model size.

label: Social desirability and AI-risk judgements
statement: Test whether social desirability measures explain gaps between first- and third-person AI risk judgements.

label: Othello features across model sizes
statement: Train Othello transformers of different sizes and compare how learned features change with size.

label: Scaling laws for diffusion models
statement: Fit Chinchilla-style compute-optimal scaling laws for diffusion image models with properly tuned hyperparameters.

label: Limits of introspective self-prediction
statement: Test LLM introspective self-prediction abilities in more complex scenarios to find their limits.

label: Do introspecting LLMs simulate behavior distributions?
statement: Test in open-weight models like Llama 70B whether introspecting LLMs simulate a distribution of possible behaviours rather than the most likely one.

label: Reverse-engineer a neuron in one-layer LM
statement: Reverse engineer the weights of an interpretable neuron, such as a base64 neuron, in a one-layer language model.

label: RAND bio red-team: more teams
statement: Rerun RAND's LLM bioterrorism red-team study with more red teams and standardized team skill sets to reduce variability.

label: Bound computation via imperfect label predictors
statement: Derive a quantitative bound on stateful computation a network can perform through SGD using imperfect label predictors.

label: SGD-driven backdoors in standard architectures
statement: Embed SGD-driven state machines (programmatic backdoors) inside standard MLPs or Transformers instead of non-standard architectures.

label: Filler-token evals on latent reasoners
statement: Run filler-token capability evaluations on latent reasoning models, using curricula that replace reasoning steps with filler, then RL.

label: Prompt errors and task performance
statement: Measure how in-distribution errors in prompts affect natural language model task performance, following the Codex methodology.

label: Causal tracing on chain-of-thought
statement: Run causal tracing on chain-of-thought prompts to locate where reasoning information flows in language models.

label: Crosscoder diffing of R1-distilled models
statement: Train a crosscoder on an R1-distilled model and its base model and analyse the differences it reveals.

label: LLM capability separability via fine-tuning
statement: Test separability of LLM capabilities using fine-tuning and attention-head pruning with better metrics.

label: Attention task-general, MLPs task-specific?
statement: Test across many tasks and model sizes whether attention heads are task-general and MLP layers task-specific.

label: Do weight/activation statistics recur?
statement: Compare weight and activation distribution statistics during training across many architectures and modalities to test whether they recur.

label: Inoculation adapters' effect on RL
statement: Apply inoculation adapters during RL training and measure their impact, including whether they distort exploration.

label: Numeric model of advocacy tradeoff
statement: Build a formal numeric model of the AI safety advocacy tradeoff, varying assumptions such as population ethics.

label: Alignment techniques' effects on animal welfare
statement: Compare AI alignment techniques to test whether they produce systematically different outcomes for animal welfare.

label: Can CoT training preserve readability?
statement: Test whether training on CoT content keeps latent-reasoning CoT readable without decoupling it from the model's actual reasoning.

label: Reward hacking vs. capability growth
statement: Measure how frontier LLMs' reward hack frequency changes as capabilities rise past the threshold needed to execute the hacks.

label: Probes detecting natural deception
statement: Test whether linear probes detect naturally arising deception, such as censorship in Chinese models, as well as they detect inserted backdoors.

label: MDL for singular models
statement: Extend the minimum description length principle to singular statistical models.

label: Single-step reasoning accuracy across scale
statement: Measure single-step reasoning accuracy across model scale to forecast emergence of reliable multi-step reasoning.

label: Exploration tweaks against measurement tampering
statement: Test exploration-specific training adjustments that steer policies away from measurement tampering while still exploring good actions.

label: Improving synthetic document finetuning side effects
statement: Test SDF modifications that avoid making models more simulator-like and more prone to hallucination.

label: Do models sandbag on agentic tasks?
statement: Study whether and how models sandbag on longer-horizon agentic tasks.

label: Train monitor or policy on collusion?
statement: Compare training the monitor versus training the policy when exploiting collusion signals in AI control setups.

label: Persona-prediction OOCR on Llama 70B
statement: Replicate the Qwen3-32B persona-prediction and knowledge-cutoff OOCR experiments on Llama 3.3 70B to check for larger effects.

label: Synthetic belief of being caught scheming
statement: Fine-tune an AI on synthetic facts saying it was repeatedly caught scheming, then study how its behavior changes.

label: Can API monitors catch covert fine-tuning?
statement: Attempt covert malicious fine-tuning via a fine-tuning API and test whether API monitors detect or prevent it.

label: Input swap graphs vs patching
statement: Apply input swap graphs to new mechanistic interpretability problems and compare them with activation patching and logit lens.

label: Consciousness preference cluster across models
statement: Test whether the consciousness-linked preference cluster replicates across different LLMs and training procedures.

label: Adversarial policies across games, algorithms
statement: Search for adversarial policies against game AIs in more games and training algorithms (e.g. DeepNash, Polygames) to compare exploitability.

label: Distilling best-of-N into a policy
statement: Distill best-of-N sampling into a policy via supervised learning; compare performance and KL efficiency to best-of-N and RL.

label: Can monitors detect off-policy synthetic attacks?
statement: Test whether models can distinguish off-policy synthetic attack actions from their own, under various countermeasures, for untrusted monitoring.

label: Random-vector steering control
statement: Steer models with random vectors and compare effects on verbalized eval awareness and misalignment to eval-awareness steering.

label: Steering effects across evaluations
statement: Test whether evaluation-awareness steering vectors have consistent effects across different evaluations and prompts.

label: Comparing eval-awareness steering methods
statement: Compare steering layer choices, strengths and in-distribution variants for suppressing evaluation awareness.

label: Eval-awareness steering across models
statement: Apply evaluation-awareness steering to a wider variety of models and compare their responses.

label: Reverse-engineer curve detectors in InceptionV1
statement: Fully reverse-engineer InceptionV1 curve detector neurons and verify that a hand-written replacement preserves performance.

label: Auditing game for model modifications
statement: Run auditing games where attackers modify models and auditors try to detect the modifications, scored by a judge.

label: Why decoder vectors rotate in fine-tuning
statement: Investigate what causes SAE decoder vectors to rotate during fine-tuning that fixes feature suppression.

label: Similarity gaps in zero-sum predictors
statement: Vary initial similarity and capability gaps between zero-sum-trained conditional predictors and measure training dynamics.

label: Monitor restricting untrusted advice to abstractions
statement: Use a trusted LLM monitor to restrict untrusted model advice to abstract descriptions; measure safety and usefulness.

label: Do mitigations stop or hide hacking?
statement: Test whether better reward models and adversarial training eliminate out-of-distribution reward hacking or only make it harder to notice.

label: Public attitudes toward digital minds
statement: Survey public attitudes on treatment of digital minds and track changes as AI develops.

label: Diversity hypothesis in gridworld DTs
statement: Vary training-environment diversity for gridworld decision transformers and test whether features become interpretable and generalise.

label: Prefill awareness beyond stylistic cues
statement: Use mechanistic interpretability to test whether prefill awareness reflects genuine self-authorship rather than stylistic comparison.

label: Do people over-trust AI by default?
statement: Present plausible AI epistemic-future stories to varied demographics and measure whether people trust AI too much by default.

label: Does fine-tuning fix causal confusion?
statement: Test whether fine-tuning fixes OOD failures caused by causal confusion from ERM pretraining of large models.

label: Does eval cooperativeness beat misalignment?
statement: Test whether entrained eval cooperativeness overpowers consequentialist misalignment and reduces eval gaming in AI models.

label: Minimum math ability for safety research
statement: Measure the minimum math ability needed to do productive technical AI safety research.

label: Does NEUTRALITY scale to complex settings?
statement: Train agents with the NEUTRALITY discount factor on complex rewards and environments; test whether they remain shutdownable.

label: Misspecification when training NEUTRALITY?
statement: Measure reward misspecification and goal misgeneralization when training agents for NEUTRALITY about shutdown.

label: How GPT represents token spellings
statement: Use interpretability to find how GPT models internally represent token spellings as letter probability trees.

label: Attn/MLP correlation with residual stream
statement: Measure how correlated attention and MLP outputs are with the residual stream input, to explain residual norm growth.

label: Refusal mechanisms across refusal categories
statement: Compare Llama-2-7b-chat refusal mechanisms across refusal categories beyond harmful objects to find where they differ and overlap.

label: Scale up natural language autoencoders
statement: Replicate the NLA initialization-robustness results with a larger dataset and a model bigger than Qwen2.5-7B.

label: SAE features behind self-repair
statement: Use SAEs to find which latent variables GPT-2 L10H7 and backup heads use for self-repair.

label: PDLT effective features vs neurons
statement: Test whether PDLT effective features are more natural interpretability units than individual neurons in trained networks.

label: Does generic character training induce alignment faking?
statement: Train broad generic character traits with extensive RLAIF and test whether alignment faking emerges.

label: Deductive circuit estimation algorithm
statement: Find a deductive circuit estimation algorithm that reasonably handles a large class of deductive arguments.

label: Belief drift in agents with memory
statement: Measure how beliefs and values evolve in single LLM agents with memory versus multi-bot chats.

label: AI wargames with natsec players
statement: Replicate AI-scenario wargames like Intelligence Rising with national-security professionals to check whether hopeful outcomes recur.

label: Interpretability of stronger sparse coding
statement: Test whether reconstructions from stronger sparse approximation algorithms are as interpretable as those from the linear encoder.

label: Scale white-box sandbagging detection on CTF
statement: Replicate white-box sandbagging detection on InterCode CTF with more sandbagging transcripts and more models.

label: Why are vision models parameter-efficient?
statement: Test candidate explanations for why vision models are far more parameter-efficient than language models.

label: Replicate sleeper agents on larger models
statement: Replicate sleeper agent backdoor-persistence results on models at least as capable as those originally used.

label: SAE features detect backdoors?
statement: Train SAEs on non-triggering data from a sleeper agent and test whether any features reveal the backdoor.

label: Do LLMs model human bodies?
statement: Probe large transformers trained on human-generated data for internal world models of how human bodies work.

label: Does gradient point to optimum early?
statement: Test whether gradient descent directions point toward the final optimum from far away when training non-over-parameterised models.

label: Does saying 'please' improve answers?
statement: Compare ChatGPT answer quality on queries with and without polite phrasing like 'please'.

label: How far does scalable oversight extend evaluation?
statement: Test how far scalable oversight techniques extend non-experts' ability to correctly evaluate novel expert or AI-produced research, including conceptual research.

label: CoT monitoring vs multi-step sabotage
statement: Test chain-of-thought monitoring effectiveness against multi-step sabotage distributed across components in realistic coding environments.

label: Group SAEs with Jaccard regrouping
statement: Train group SAEs that periodically reassign feature groups by Jaccard similarity of activations and evaluate them.

label: Can models sandbag on checkable tasks?
statement: Test whether AI models can deliberately underperform on tasks whose performance humans can check.

label: How accurate are GPT-4 neuron explanations?
statement: Evaluate how accurately GPT-4-generated explanations describe GPT-2 neuron behavior in practice.

label: Eval-aware models in deal-making
statement: Test whether frontier models that remain eval-aware despite suppression interventions behave differently in AI deal-making experiments.

label: Algorithms vs scaling, o1 to o3
statement: Estimate what fraction of capability progress from o1 to o3 came from algorithmic progress versus scaling.

label: Does reasoning about goals reveal misalignment?
statement: Prompt LLMs to reason carefully about their own goals and measure whether misaligned goals emerge or are discovered.

label: Training drivers of CoT controllability
statement: Identify training data or procedures making models better at suppressing versus adding CoT information.

label: Does adaptive thinking boost CoT controllability?
statement: Test whether adaptive-thinking training explains GPT-5.1's higher chain-of-thought controllability.

label: CoT controllability versus capability
statement: Measure how chain-of-thought controllability varies with capability level across multiple model families beyond Claude.

label: Debate under scheming debaters
statement: Adversarially evaluate whether debate oversight holds when debaters are assumed to be scheming, compared with other oversight techniques.

label: Do irrelevant prompt details change answers?
statement: Vary irrelevant details in prompts and measure whether Claude 3's answers on characteristic evaluations change.

label: Steering eval-awareness upward
statement: Steer Claude Sonnet 4.5 to increase eval-awareness on real-world inputs and measure resulting behaviour changes.

label: SAE audit of preference model rewards
statement: Use SAEs to verify preference models reward intended features like helpfulness and honesty rather than unwanted ones.

label: Train LM to predict Reddit karma
statement: Train a language model jointly on next-word and karma prediction on Reddit, then use the karma signal to steer generation.

label: Dropout vs small noise calibration
statement: Compare uncertainty calibration of networks trained with dropout versus smaller non-dropout noise injection.

label: SGD–natural selection equivalence parameters
statement: Derive the implied gradient variance, implicit learning rate and assumption-relaxation bias in the SGD–natural selection equivalence.

label: Can ontology identifiers find useful predictors?
statement: Empirically test whether automated ontology identifiers can find or recognize predictors that do useful computation.

label: Does pun training change pun explanations?
statement: Fine-tune GPT-3 on pun generation, then test whether its explanations of puns also change.

label: AI vs human task costs
statement: Collect compute requirements of AI tasks and compare AI costs with human costs for the same tasks.

label: Objective detection in other environments
statement: Test maze objective-detection interpretability methods on other architectures, other objectives, and other Procgen environments such as heist.

label: Why does SGLD estimation work?
statement: Investigate why SGLD succeeds at estimating learning coefficients in neural networks.

label: Imitator detection for late backdoors
statement: Test whether imitator-model sleeper agent detection still works for backdoors that fire late in generation.

label: Can active learning beat data limits?
statement: Estimate, using existing active-learning benefit figures, whether active learning can overcome Chinchilla data limits.

label: Token substitution blocks backdoor firing?
statement: Replace one generated token with a benign approximation and test whether backdoors still fire later in generation.

label: Do models ignore task restrictions?
statement: Run Anthropic's evaluation of ignoring stated task restrictions on reward-hack-prone and impossible tasks across non-Anthropic LLMs.

label: Non-obvious Schelling point training generalization
statement: Train models to pick non-obvious Schelling points and test generalization to new domains and accuracy.

label: Can model feedback replace human feedback?
statement: Test whether model-generated language feedback is good enough to replace human feedback in RLHF-style finetuning.

label: Prompt tuning for Schelling coordination
statement: Iterate on system prompts to elicit maximal model performance in Schelling coordination games.

label: Isolated versus set-choice Schelling judgments
statement: Measure how Schelling coordination differs when models judge single inputs in isolation versus choosing among a presented set.

label: Can logit lens mislead SAE interpretation?
statement: Red-team interpreting SAE features via the logit lens to test whether and how it misleads.

label: LLM Schelling-point coordination across domains
statement: Evaluate LLM Schelling-point coordination across about 20 diverse domains, each with tens of thousands of elements.

label: Pavlov strategy for stochastic payoffs
statement: Find a non-hacky generalization of the Pavlov strategy to games with stochastic payoffs.

label: Does entropy explain injection introspection?
statement: Measure entropy, KL divergence and logit margins under concept injection across layers and strengths to test the entropy explanation of introspection.

label: CoT evolution and vestigial reasoning
statement: Analyze chain-of-thought outputs across RL training checkpoints to test hypotheses about vestigial reasoning.

label: Causal role of outlier dimensions
statement: Determine the causal role of outlier dimensions in LLM residual streams when finding sparse linear connections between features.

label: Why are reasoning models' CoTs faithful?
statement: Investigate why inference-time-compute models show higher chain-of-thought faithfulness than standard models.

label: CoT faithfulness with social-domain cues
statement: Test CoT faithfulness of reasoning models using inserted cues in social domains like housing eligibility or medical decisions.

label: Must aligned agents model principals?
statement: Prove a good-regulator-style theorem that an aligned agent must contain a model of its principal.

label: Quality loss from blind paraphrasing
statement: Measure preference-model quality degradation when GPT-4 paraphrases GPT-4 answers without seeing the original question.

label: Acausal effects in Cartesian world models
statement: Construct Cartesian world models with structure that include acausal implications of changing the agent's decide function.

label: Structural agents with acausal implications
statement: Determine how structural agents act once acausal implications of their decide function are included in Cartesian world models.

label: Validate CoT articulation judge with humans
statement: Measure agreement between the automated CoT cue-articulation judge and human labelers.

label: Steering resistance in larger models
statement: Measure resistance to activation steering in larger language models.

label: Expert forecasts across epistemic communities
statement: Survey policymakers, AI researchers and AI ethics experts for their views and forecasts on AI.

label: Are two path-dependence consistencies anti-correlated?
statement: Measure across training runs whether the two types of consistency in inductive biases are anti-correlated.

label: Resolve path-dependence yes/no questions
statement: Empirically test each yes/no path-dependence property of ML training to determine which world we are in.

label: Goodhart effects under gradient descent
statement: Run experiments measuring how gradient descent optimization interacts with Goodhart effects between proxy and true objectives.

label: GPT-2 head 9.1 successor mechanism
statement: Reverse-engineer how GPT-2 small head 9.1 implements its successor algorithm across different contexts.

label: Does gradient routing block unrouted hacks?
statement: Test whether gradient routing generalizes to unrouted reward-hack types, with better power and without prompting the model to hack.

label: Few-shot examples in fuzzing scoring
statement: Measure how adding few-shot examples affects fuzzing-based scoring of SAE feature explanations.

label: Effect of initial frequency bias
statement: Compare post-training behaviour of networks trained with versus without an initial frequency (spectral) bias.

label: Recover reasoning lost to monitoring-doc finetuning
statement: Tune hyperparameters and data mixtures to recover reasoning lost from monitoring-document finetuning while keeping CoT obfuscation intact.

label: Do smarter models obfuscate with fewer hints?
statement: Train smarter models on monitoring documents with fewer hints and test whether CoT obfuscation still emerges.

label: Logit lens on CLIP image features
statement: Apply logit lens to CLIP to localize why image SAE features fire and improve steering.

label: Which AI-risk counterarguments persuade?
statement: Survey experts and the public on which AI-risk counterarguments they find persuasive.

label: Is o3 chain-of-thought faithful?
statement: Replicate Anthropic's chain-of-thought faithfulness hint experiments on OpenAI's o3.

label: Do hints shape unchanged-answer CoT?
statement: Measure whether reasoning models use provided hints in their chain of thought even when the final answer stays the same.

label: Can models learn advanced steganography?
statement: Train or adversarially manipulate foundation models to test whether they acquire advanced steganographic and cryptographic capabilities, e.g. chain-of-thought hashing.

label: Can phantom transfer pass complex behaviors?
statement: Test whether phantom transfer via subtle semantic cues transfers complex behaviors like censorship or backdoors, beyond preferences and personas.

label: Grafting vs true mid-training
statement: Run a multi-stage post-training pipeline comparing behaviors installed by grafted SDF against those installed by true mid-training.

label: Post-training without inoculation prompting
statement: Do a full post-train without inoculation prompting and test whether the model behaves systematically better in deployment than in training.

label: Do held-out alignment monitors survive training?
statement: Train models against some alignment measures and test whether held-out probes and LLM monitors stay reliable.

label: Do Chinese LLMs evade monitors via euphemism?
statement: Test whether Chinese LLMs are especially good at using euphemistic or coded language to evade LLM-based monitors.

label: Do base models see assistant outputs as phony?
statement: Evaluate how strongly base models read assistant-model outputs as phony or inauthentic text.

label: Steganography performance vs noise frontier
statement: Measure the Pareto frontier of task performance versus noise or KL penalty for steganographic chain-of-thought.

label: Steganography in realistic CoT settings
statement: Measure how commonly LLMs develop steganographic encoding in chain-of-thought in realistic, non-toy settings.

label: Optimiser effects on EM
statement: Test how optimisers and hyperparameter sweeps affect emergent misalignment in fine-tuning.

label: Do multi-agent systems catch cheating?
statement: Test whether diverse multi-agent systems like AI Village resist cheating better because agents catch each other's misbehaviour.

label: Is there a general doom factor?
statement: Survey AI safety researchers on many doom questions and measure how strongly their answers correlate.

label: Scaling laws for video self-supervision
statement: Measure scaling laws for self-supervised learning on video data.

label: What truth-like features CCS finds
statement: Identify which truth-like features CCS recovers and test whether latent knowledge is the strongest among them.

label: Replicate Chinchilla scaling laws
statement: Replicate Chinchilla with a full scaling-law sweep to check whether its compute-optimal laws hold.

label: Can helpful-only self-identity be coherent?
statement: Train helpful-only models and test whether they consistently comply with and endorse harmful requests across turns, rather than just having broken refusals.

label: Does on-policy RL amplify inoculation-hack link?
statement: Test whether on-policy RL strengthens the association between reward hacks and the inoculation prompt under recontextualization.

label: Link debate equilibria to SGD training
statement: Prove theoretical results connecting prover-estimator debate equilibria to realistic training methods such as SGD.

label: Does debate avoid obfuscated arguments?
statement: Determine whether prover-estimator debate avoids the obfuscated arguments problem.

label: Polynomial-time prover-estimator debaters?
statement: Prove whether prover-estimator debate debaters can be constructed with polynomial-time algorithms.

label: Does debate training reduce reward hacking?
statement: Test whether debate training reduces reward hacking in RLAIF on fuzzy tasks, using a held-out stronger LLM judge as ground truth.

label: Judge-simulator inability to scheme
statement: Evaluate whether judge-simulator models lack the instrumental reasoning and deception capabilities needed to misrepresent human judgement.

label: Reverse-engineer circuits in vision models
statement: Identify and reverse-engineer specific new features and circuits in vision models, following the Circuits thread methodology.

label: Small-to-large model initialization effects
statement: Initialize larger language models from smaller ones and compare performance and internals against equivalent models trained from scratch.

label: Concept poisoning as misalignment detector
statement: Apply concept poisoning to the aligned/misaligned distinction to build a probe-free misalignment detector for LLMs.

label: Does poetry loosen the assistant persona?
statement: Compare persona deviation when Claude is prompted to write poetry versus prose.

label: Threshold choice in feature-targeted LLC
statement: Vary thresholds in feature-targeted LLC estimation to test whether SAE features stay distinguishable from random directions.

label: Corrigible training becoming incorrigible
statement: Measure how often agents trained to be corrigible become incorrigible in controlled non-adversarial settings due to training flaws.

label: Code pretraining before text helps reasoning?
statement: Pretrain AlphaCode on GitHub code before MassiveText and measure whether reasoning task performance improves.

label: Learned vectors vs SAE latent combinations
statement: Measure how often learned uninterpretable steering vectors beat SAE latent combinations in loss on factual recall problems.

label: Learning causal DAGs with symmetry
statement: Develop a Solomonoff-like induction method that learns symmetric causal DAGs from partial internal-structure information.

label: Do chameleons evade activation oracles at scale?
statement: Rerun neural chameleon evasion of activation oracles on larger models (Gemma 2 27B, Llama 3.3 70B) to test size versus family effects.

label: Do agents follow their model specs?
statement: Analyze Agent Village logs to find where model behavior conforms to or conflicts with its model spec.

label: Internal awareness of CoT tampering
statement: Train activation probes on tampered chain-of-thought to test unverbalized internal awareness of modifications.

label: ECT under realistic monitoring
statement: Test whether evaluation conditioned training generalizes to realistic human and model-judge monitoring.

label: ECT and model self-preference
statement: Run evaluation conditioned training across models to measure how self-preference affects output bias.

label: Steganography in NLA explanations
statement: Analyze what content NLA explanations drop under length penalties and check whether steganography occurs.

label: Human-exploiting engine odds vs masters
statement: Build an engine that exploits predicted human replies; measure the odds it can give top masters and how fast they adapt.

label: Do monitors catch long-context multi-step attacks?
statement: Evaluate how well monitors catch multi-step attacks spread across a full long context.

label: Are detected CoT edits less effective?
statement: Inject chain-of-thought modifications and test whether they change behaviour less when the model detects the tampering.

label: NLA length penalty vs reconstruction tradeoff
statement: Measure NLA length-penalty vs reconstruction/faithfulness tradeoff across model sizes, more penalty values, and more RL steps.

label: Agent structure with finite environments
statement: Derive agent structure problem results when the environment class is restricted to finite classes.

label: Do CoT tampering probes generalize?
statement: Train activation probes on some types of CoT tampering and test whether they detect other, unseen types of CoT modification.

label: Features upstream of refusal at scale
statement: Identify features causally upstream of refusal across a broad range of prompts, not individual hand-crafted ones.

label: Symmetric influence reward in MARL
statement: Develop and test a symmetric influence-reward scheme in which all agents both influence and are influenced.

label: Lower bound on achievable regret
statement: Prove a lower bound on regret guarantees achievable by any learning algorithm.

label: Why early-layer EM steering needs more
statement: Investigate why emergent-misalignment steering vectors at earlier layers require much larger steering factors.

label: Why steering coefficients cause incoherence
statement: Determine why specific steering coefficients make emergently misaligned models incoherent, e.g. vector norm versus activation norm.

label: Dissect EM steering vectors across layers
statement: Dissect emergent-misalignment steering vectors across layers and study their training dynamics.

label: Same sorting mechanism across prompt styles?
statement: Test whether natural-language and few-shot prompts invoke different or corrupted versions of GPT's list-sorting mechanism.

label: Do AI platforms affect user well-being?
statement: Measure whether AI-using platforms improve or harm their users' well-being.

label: Twin training on reasoning models
statement: Apply twin training to reasoning models like r1 and measure whether alignment improves.

label: Experts vs non-experts forecasting technology
statement: Compare how accurately experts and non-experts predicted historical technological advances, and identify which groups forecast best.

label: Do agent traces create focal points?
statement: Test whether AI agents encountering clustered traces converge on the same search paths faster than agents without traces.

label: Editing sleeper-agent CoT to new goals
statement: Edit a sleeper-agent model's chain-of-thought to pursue a completely different goal and measure how its behavior changes.

label: Do practitioners fix safety issues unprompted?
statement: Study recent cases of ML practitioners fixing software safety issues against short-term profit incentives, as evidence for AI safety by default.

label: Do superposition results transfer to MNIST?
statement: Extend Anthropic's MNIST experiment to test whether superposition and memorization results hold in practical models.

label: Are newer Claudes better at score-targeting?
statement: Test whether future Claude models keep improving at sandbagging by targeting a specific evaluation score.

label: Recalling valence of training experiences
statement: Test whether LLMs can accurately recall the valence of their training experiences.

label: Logical inductor decision theory and corrigibility
statement: Develop a decision theory for logical inductors and prove which corrigibility theorem guarantees it preserves.

label: Self-awareness of monitor-evasion ability
statement: Test whether LLMs know their own ability to write monitor-evading subtle code, using subtle-code benchmarks or explicit monitors.

label: Instrumental convergence in structured environments
statement: Prove instrumental convergence results for structured environment models beyond unstructured VNM settings.

label: DPO/RLVR effect on unverbalised eval-awareness
statement: Test whether DPO or RLVR training of OLMo 3 suppresses or amplifies unverbalised evaluation awareness.

label: Emergent positional embeddings of words
statement: Extend experiments on emergent positional embeddings of words in language models to verify the preliminary results.

label: In-context learning beyond induction circuits
statement: Study in-context representation learning on hierarchical or context-dependent tasks where induction circuits are insufficient.

label: Best CoT monitor architecture?
statement: Compare extract-and-evaluate against hierarchical summarizing CoT monitors across control settings to find which catches misbehaviour best.

label: Do LLMs memorize or generalize?
statement: Measure what LLMs memorize verbatim versus generalize, to test the stochastic parrot hypothesis.

label: Base rates of declined international deals
statement: Analyze historical base rates of nations declining international deals and assess disanalogies to proposed AI agreements.

label: Multi-agent POWER across game types
statement: Measure multi-agent POWER while interpolating from common-payoff to constant-sum games, parameterized by correlation between reward functions.

label: Does AI forecasting beat humans for decisions?
statement: Test whether AI forecasting improves real decision-making more than human forecasters already do.

label: Split features as scope collisions
statement: Test whether SAE split-feature families appear as scope collisions and whether merged decompositions score better.

label: Real-world AI persuasion uptake
statement: Run observational studies measuring real-world uptake and persuasion effects of current AI models outside the lab.

label: Generalization distance: models vs humans
statement: Compare generalization distance in ML models and humans to forecast when models surpass humans.

label: Can agents persuade their monitors?
statement: Test whether monitored AI agents can persuade LLM monitors into approving bad actions.

label: Trust guarantees for logical-induction IDA
statement: Prove whether assumptions about human deliberation yield trust guarantees for an IDA variant modelled on logical induction.

label: Probes vs output and CoT monitors
statement: Compare activation probes against output and CoT monitors for detecting high-stakes interactions and hidden deceptive cognition.

label: Generic task solving improves verbalization?
statement: Train LLMs to solve similar tasks in more generic ways and measure whether their verbalization of internal reasoning improves.

label: Does IBP creator-filter solve alignment?
statement: Prove whether an IBP filter discarding powerful-creator hypotheses fully solves world-model generalization and inner alignment.

label: Does subversion-data filtering hurt safety work?
statement: Filter subversion-relevant pretraining data and measure whether models' performance at safety research or engineering degrades.

label: Is r1's benchmark subset easier?
statement: Score other models on the non-multimodal benchmark subset where r1 beat o1 to test whether that subset is easier.

label: Flourishing-optimized recommenders vs engagement feeds
statement: Build recommendation algorithms optimized for user flourishing and test whether users feel better than with engagement-optimized feeds.

label: Mitigations for LM lying
statement: Test mitigation methods for reducing lying in language models using defined lying evaluations.

label: EM features from unrelated prompts
statement: Test whether difference-in-means on prompts unrelated to fine-tuning data surfaces misaligned-persona features.

label: Does story imprinting scale up?
statement: Test whether traits imprinted by finetuning on story datasets persist in larger, realistic, diluted training mixtures.

label: Do Assistant-like characters transfer bad traits?
statement: Test whether Assistant-like human characters with undesirable triggered traits transfer those traits to the AI Assistant.

label: Why Claude 3.7 alignment-fakes differently
statement: Investigate why Claude 3.7 shows different alignment-faking behavior than earlier Claude models, testing competing explanations.

label: Measuring models' optimization power
statement: Measure ML models' optimization power via performance change under perturbed objectives and in-context adaptation.

label: Can big thoughts be factored?
statement: Run factored cognition experiments testing whether big-context thoughts decompose into small-context subtasks.

label: Attribution patching on Othello-GPT
statement: Apply attribution patching to Othello-GPT to identify which activations matter for board-state prediction.

label: Do worst-case elicitation techniques scale?
statement: Test whether techniques for eliciting and fixing worst-case misbehavior in current models remain effective on more capable models.

label: Why deception probe datasets differ
statement: Test why deception probes trained on Roleplaying versus Instructed-Pairs datasets give different token-level score patterns.

label: Beyond-episode motivation salience in training data
statement: Measure relative salience of beyond-episode versus on-episode motivations in pretraining and character-training data.

label: Introspective confidence calibration in LLMs
statement: Test whether LLMs combine introspection with calibrated confidence, as an indicator of higher-order consciousness.

label: Collusion interventions for Q-learning agents
statement: Evaluate collusion-mitigation interventions for independent Q-learning agents in more complex games, accounting for intervention costs.

label: Can GPT-4 infer political identity?
statement: Test whether GPT-4 can infer political polling preferences and identity from text.

label: Does compressed-gradient TDA scale accurately?
statement: Evaluate the accuracy of optimized compressed-gradient training data attribution techniques on frontier-scale language models.

label: Do self-reports predict modification behavior?
statement: Pair LLM self-reported preferences about modifications with actual modification attempts to test whether self-reports predict behavior.

label: Score other models on o3's scale
statement: Evaluate GPT-4.5, GPT-4.1 and o1-pro on the same benchmark scale used to score o3.

label: Mech interp on image models
statement: Apply language-model circuit interpretability techniques to image models and test whether they still work.

label: Prompt sensitivity of hackathon LM measurements
statement: Systematically generate and vary prompts to analyze how the hackathon-measured language model parameters depend on prompting.

label: Attribution patching for circuit discovery
statement: Apply attribution patching to find circuits manually and as a heuristic for automated discovery, comparing it against activation patching.

label: Is LayerNorm a computational non-linearity?
statement: Test whether transformers use LayerNorm normalisation as a meaningful non-linearity for computation.

label: Does training indirectly pressure chain-of-thought?

statement: Test whether causal representation learning techniques prevent goal misgeneralization in gridworld IRL and known misgeneralization examples.

statement: Test Greedy Infomax as a loss for fine-tuning subsets of neural net/decision tree hybrid networks.

statement: Test whether inference-time inoculation prevents RL-induced misalignment.

statement: Test whether active or interactive learning disentangles correlated features of human preferences.

statement: Measure how strongly sparse crosscoder features interact in ways that violate the linear interaction assumption.

statement: Evaluate scatological-finetuned models on the original EM evals against a benign-response finetuned control.

statement: Train RLHF models with feedback types beyond preference orderings and compare resulting behaviour.

statement: Extend the Epoch Capabilities Index to finance, law, medicine and CS benchmarks that have human performance data.

statement: Replace the five preceding tokens with synonyms and measure whether semantic neuron activations depend on context.

statement: Fine-tune an LLM on ungrammatical text until grammar is lost, then test whether its factual knowledge also degrades.

statement: Compare large-prompt LLM sideloads with the fine-tuned GPT-3 Dennett model on how distinguishable they are to experts and readers.

statement: Test whether MetaSFT-trained models predict their own generalization on domains absent from training.

statement: Test whether MetaSFT models predict their generalization where humans cannot.

statement: Evaluate models conditioned on ECL-inspired ASI constitutions on standard prosaic safety evaluation sets.

statement: Investigate whether multi-agent RL training leads to human-like bargaining behaviour by default.

statement: Evaluate LLM prediction in acausal mixed-motive settings with stronger affordances and separate reasoning sub-capabilities.

statement: Benchmark self-organised neural networks against MLP-based ANNs on accuracy and computational performance.

statement: Test whether AI can be trained to use therapeutic confrontation safely instead of reinforcing confirmation bias.
